summary.en: Turn raw bytes into structured records by parsing CSV, JSON, and binary formats by hand.
summary.zh-TW: 親手解析 CSV、JSON 與二進位格式，把原始位元組轉成結構化資料。

summary.en: The layer that actually puts bytes on disk: log-structured merge trees, B-trees, and page management.
summary.zh-TW: 真正把資料寫到磁碟的那一層：LSM-tree、B-tree 與頁面管理。

summary.en: Data structures that make lookups fast: hash indexes, B-trees, and LSM indexes.
summary.zh-TW: 讓查詢變快的資料結構：雜湊索引、B-tree 與 LSM 索引。

summary.en: Parse, plan, optimise, and execute queries over your data, from SQL text to a result set.
summary.zh-TW: 解析、規劃、最佳化並執行查詢：從 SQL 文字到結果集。

summary.en: Assemble storage, indexes, transactions, and a query layer into a working database.
summary.zh-TW: 把儲存、索引、交易與查詢層組裝成一個可運作的資料庫。

summary.en: Keep hot data close with eviction policies, TTLs, and write strategies.
summary.zh-TW: 用淘汰策略、TTL 與寫入策略把熱資料放在近處。

summary.en: Decouple producers from consumers with durable logs, delivery guarantees, and offsets.
summary.zh-TW: 用持久化日誌、傳遞保證與位移，把生產者與消費者解耦。

summary.en: Compute over unbounded data with windows, watermarks, state, and exactly-once semantics.
summary.zh-TW: 在無界資料上運算：視窗、浮水印、狀態與 exactly-once 語意。

summary.en: Schedule and coordinate multi-step pipelines with dependencies, retries, and backfills.
summary.zh-TW: 以相依關係、重試與回補，排程並協調多步驟管線。

summary.en: Assert what your data should look like with schema checks, constraints, and validation rules.
summary.zh-TW: 用 schema 檢查、約束與驗證規則，為資料立下應有的樣貌。

summary.en: Detect freshness, volume, and distribution problems before your dashboards mislead you.
summary.zh-TW: 在儀表板誤導你之前，偵測新鮮度、資料量與分佈的問題。

summary.en: Build inverted indexes, tokenizers, and ranking to search text at speed.
summary.zh-TW: 打造反向索引、斷詞器與排序，快速搜尋文字。

summary.en: Store embeddings and find nearest neighbours with approximate search structures.
summary.zh-TW: 儲存嵌入向量，並以近似搜尋結構找出最近鄰。

summary.en: Columnar storage, vectorised execution, and analytics at scale over large datasets.
summary.zh-TW: 欄式儲存、向量化執行，對大型資料集進行規模化分析。

summary.en: Replication, consensus, partitioning, and fault tolerance across many machines.
summary.zh-TW: 在多台機器間處理複製、共識、分區與容錯。

learningOutcomes: Navigate row groups and column chunks
entries.summary: The official specification for Parquet's columnar layout, covering row groups, column chunks, pages, encodings, and metadata, with enough detail to write your own reader or writer.
entries.title: Apache Parquet File Format

entries.summary: A focused tutorial that indexes a large document set in Go by building an inverted index with tokenization, filtering, and boolean queries, small enough to read in one sitting.
entries.title: Let's Build a Full-Text Search Engine

learningOutcomes: Design an append-friendly B+tree on disk
Add tables, indexes, and simple transactions
entries.summary: An online book that builds a persistent, copy-on-write B+tree database in Go, then layers a relational-style query interface and transactions on top.
entries.title: Build Your Own Database From Scratch (Go)

learningOutcomes: Build a non-blocking TCP event loop
Implement core data structures and key expiry
entries.summary: An online book that recreates a Redis-like in-memory server from sockets up: an event loop, the RESP protocol, hash tables, sorted sets, and TTL-based key expiry.
entries.title: Build Your Own Redis with C/C++

entries.summary: A university course whose projects have you implement the internals of a disk-based database, including a buffer pool, a B+tree index, query operators, and concurrency control, inside the BusTub teaching system.
entries.title: CMU 15-445: Database Systems

entries.summary: A course focused on the internals of modern analytical databases: columnar storage, vectorized and compiled execution, and query optimization, the building blocks of a data warehouse engine.
entries.title: CMU 15-721: Advanced Database Systems

learningOutcomes: Walk and evaluate an abstract syntax tree
entries.summary: A complete, free book that builds two interpreters for a small language; its scanning and parsing chapters are a superb, practical grounding for writing any file-format or query parser.
entries.title: Crafting Interpreters

learningOutcomes: Reason about consistency and consensus trade-offs
entries.summary: A widely used reference that maps the whole landscape, from storage engines and replication to partitioning, transactions, and consensus, giving you the mental models to design and rebuild data systems.
entries.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications

prerequisites: Any language with stdin and stdout (Go recommended)
entries.summary: A set of hands-on challenges built on the Maelstrom test harness where you implement broadcast, a grow-only counter, and a replicated log, then have your solutions stress-tested against failures.
entries.title: Gossip Glomers: Distributed Systems Challenges

learningOutcomes: Implement layered HNSW insertion and search
Tune the recall versus latency trade-off
entries.summary: The paper introducing HNSW, the graph index behind most modern vector databases, a clear specification you can follow to implement fast approximate nearest-neighbor search.
entries.title: HNSW: Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs

learningOutcomes: Represent queries as logical and physical plans
Implement joins, aggregates, and a simple optimizer
entries.summary: A concise book, by a DataFusion co-creator, that builds a query engine step by step: data sources, logical plans, expression evaluation, physical operators, and a SQL front end.
entries.title: How Query Engines Work

learningOutcomes: Implement a REPL and a simple command parser
Store rows in a paged file on disk
Build a B-tree for lookups and inserts
entries.summary: A step-by-step series that grows a SQLite-style database in C, one commit at a time, from a REPL and pager to a B-tree stored on disk.
entries.title: Let's Build a Simple Database

learningOutcomes: Add bloom filters and MVCC snapshots
entries.summary: A guided tutorial that builds an LSM-tree storage engine in Rust from the ground up, including memtables, SSTables, compaction, bloom filters, and MVCC, with tests for each milestone.
entries.title: Mini-LSM: Build a Storage Engine in a Week

learningOutcomes: Build Raft leader election and log replication
Layer a replicated key-value store and sharding on Raft
entries.summary: A graduate course whose lab series has you build a fault-tolerant, replicated key-value store in Go, starting from MapReduce, through a full Raft implementation, to a sharded service.
entries.title: MIT 6.824: Distributed Systems

learningOutcomes: Append records to a log file
Read values back by file offset
entries.summary: An educational project that implements a disk-based, log-structured key-value store in Python following the Bitcask design, with a small codebase and exercises to complete.
entries.title: py-caskdb: A Bitcask-style Key-Value Store

entries.summary: The Raft home page gathers the paper, talks, and an interactive visualization that walk through leader election, log replication, and safety, the pieces you need to implement consensus yourself.
entries.title: Raft: Understandable Consensus

learningOutcomes: Model queries as an abstract syntax tree
entries.summary: A hands-on series that builds a tiny SQL engine in Go, with a lexer, a parser, and an in-memory executor for SELECT, INSERT, and CREATE, explaining each layer as it goes.
entries.title: Writing a SQL Database from Scratch

learningOutcomes: Distinguish event time from processing time
entries.summary: A foundational two-part essay that untangles streaming vocabulary, including event versus processing time, windowing, watermarks, and triggers, the concepts any stream processor must get right.
entries.title: Streaming 101: The World Beyond Batch

learningOutcomes: Model a topic as a partitioned, append-only log
Reason about offsets, retention, and replayability
prerequisites: Basic understanding of databases and messaging
entries.summary: Kafka's design documentation explains the partitioned, append-only commit log at its core, including offsets, replication, and delivery guarantees, the foundation for building a durable message queue yourself.
entries.title: Apache Kafka: Design and the Commit Log

learningOutcomes: See derived data as stream transformations
Relate change data capture to materialized views
entries.summary: A talk-turned-article that reframes materialized views, caches, and indexes as derived data kept in sync by an event log, the core idea behind log-based stream processing.
entries.title: Turning the Database Inside-Out

learningOutcomes: Explain how a B-tree index is traversed
Design indexes for common query shapes
Read execution plans to spot missing indexes
entries.summary: A free web book that teaches how database indexes actually work by reasoning about B-tree structure, then shows how query patterns, ordering, and joins decide whether an index helps.
entries.title: Use the Index, Luke!

learningOutcomes: Model time-ordered samples in memory and on disk
Partition data by time for efficient queries
Use a write-ahead log for durability
entries.summary: A hands-on tutorial that builds a time-series database engine in Go from the ground up, covering an in-memory head block, partitioning by time, a write-ahead log for durability, and querying by labels.
entries.title: Writing a Time Series Database from Scratch

steps.note: Learn to scan and parse text into a syntax tree.
See how a real columnar format lays out data on disk.
Turn parsed queries into logical and physical plans.
Put lexer, parser, and executor together over real tables.

learningPaths.summary: Start by turning bytes into structured data, then work up to planning and executing queries over it. A path from parsing to a working query engine.
learningPaths.title: From File Parser to Query Engine

steps.note: Build a single-node, log-structured key-value store.
Upgrade storage to an LSM tree with compaction.
Add a network protocol and in-memory data structures.
Learn the consensus algorithm that keeps replicas in sync.
Implement a replicated, sharded key-value store on Raft.

learningPaths.summary: Begin with a single-node store, evolve it into a durable storage engine, then replicate it across machines with consensus. A path from one key to many nodes.
learningPaths.title: From Key-Value Store to Distributed Database

steps.note: Understand the log as a unifying abstraction.
Learn windowing, event time, and watermarks.
Reframe views and caches as stream transformations.
Store time-ordered data efficiently for querying.

learningPaths.summary: Treat an append-only log as the source of truth, then compute derived views over it as data keeps arriving. A path from logging events to processing streams.
learningPaths.title: From Event Log to Stream Processor
